papers.title: Hypothalamic Orexin Neurons Modulate Sleep-Wake States and Seizure Burden in a Kainic Acid-Induced Mouse Model of Chronic Temporal Lobe Epilepsy.
papers.summary: In a kainic acid-induced chronic temporal lobe epilepsy mouse model, chemogenetic activation of hypothalamic orexin neurons increased wakefulness and seizure count/duration, while inhibition or orexin receptor 1 blockade with SB334867 promoted sleep and reduced seizure burden; chronic mice also showed state-dependent spectral remodeling and enhanced delta-high-gamma coupling partially attenuated by SB334867.

papers.title: A Temporally Causal Two-Layer Framework for Wearable EEG Sleep Staging and Short-Horizon Sleep-Transition Forecasting.
papers.summary: Developed a temporally causal two-layer framework for wearable EEG sleep staging and short-horizon sleep-transition forecasting; layer M0 achieved 0.830 accuracy and 0.704 macro-F1 across five stages, and layer M1 predicted W/N1-to-N2+ transitions with AUROC of 0.786-0.801 at 60-120 s horizons.

papers.title: Dihydromyricetin Regulates Sleep and Protects Against Oxidative Stress in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.summary: In Drosophila, dihydromyricetin increased sleep duration and modulated sleep fragmentation across young, aged, and short-sleep mutants, altered neurotransmitter-related gene expression including VGAT and Trhn, and in paraquat-induced oxidative stress models restored stress-disrupted sleep, reduced oxidative damage and intestinal apoptosis, and extended lifespan.

papers.title: Sleep EEG distinguishes learned from novel auditory cues without predicting memory retention in a targeted memory reactivation study
papers.summary: Using targeted memory reactivation in 81 healthy young adults, the authors tested whether learned versus novel auditory cues elicit distinct sleep EEG responses and whether encoding or sleep measures predict long-term retention. Learned cues produced stronger delta responses than novel sounds during NREM sleep, but TMR did not improve memory (and was linked to poorer retention of initially weak memories), while pre-sleep memory strength and encoding vividness predicted retention.

papers.title: Alternative CLOCK isoforms specify a non-circadian timing circuit in Drosophila.
papers.journal: Journal of genetics and genomics = Yi chuan xue bao
papers.summary: Using Drosophila, identified that CLK and CYC, but not PER and TIM, are required for interval timing underlying sexual experience-dependent shorter mating duration, with an ITP-LNd-centered clock-neuron circuit and short CLK isoforms lacking the canonical DNA-binding motif selectively required for this non-circadian timing behavior.

papers.title: Phox2b 25-Ala expansion leads to Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome like phenotypes in mice.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Lung cellular and molecular physiology
papers.summary: Generated and characterized a new Phox2b +5 alanine expansion mouse model reproducing congenital central hypoventilation syndrome-like phenotypes, including neonatal hypoventilation, blunted hypercapnic response, premature death in 75% of pups, reduced inspiratory activity, impaired acidosis response, and reduced phox2b-expressing retrotrapezoid nucleus neurons.

papers.title: MG-STNet: A Compact Multi-Granularity Spatiotemporal Network for Adaptive Sleep Staging.
papers.summary: MG-STNet is a compact multi-granularity spatiotemporal network for PSG sleep staging that uses parallel downsampling branches, global-local feature recalibration, adaptive spatiotemporal convolution routing, and temporal attention encoding to handle time-varying sleep rhythms. On Sleep-EDF-20 and Sleep-EDF-78 with subject-independent cross-validation, the four-channel model reached 87.3% and 84.5% accuracy with 46.6K parameters, and the single-channel version 86.6% and 83.2% with 48.6K parameters.

papers.title: GamSleepNet: A Lightweight Automatic Sleep Staging Framework Based on Gabor Feature Extraction and Mamba Sequence Modeling for Single-Channel EEG.
papers.summary: GamSleepNet is a low-parameter single-channel EEG sleep-staging framework combining improved Gabor-kernel feature extraction with a learnable filter branch and a Mamba selective state-space temporal model, plus teacher-student feature alignment and two-stage training. On Sleep-EDF with limited labeled subjects it used 30.86k parameters and achieved 87.86% overall accuracy and 82.62% macro F1 (best among compared models), with improved REM and N1 recognition and stable performance under low SNR and scarce labels.

papers.title: Revisiting the First Night Effect of Polysomnography Using Wearable EEG Headbands in Older Adults with Sleep Disturbances
papers.summary: Fifty-eight community-dwelling older adults with sleep disturbances completed up to seven nights of wearable EEG headband monitoring including one simultaneous home polysomnography night to characterize the first night effect. Polysomnography nights showed about 35 minutes more wake after sleep onset, 21 minutes less N3 sleep, and 15% lower sleep efficiency, with no differences in total sleep time or REM sleep, suggesting single-night polysomnography may overstate sleep disruption and understate deep sleep.

papers.title: Fighting Sleep: Minute-by-Minute Driver Fatigue from a Dry-Electrode EEG Headband
papers.summary: This study tested whether a four-electrode dry EEG headband (eye-movement signals plus head-tilt motion sensor) can track driver fatigue minute by minute using an untrained index referenced to each participant's first eight minutes. Across nine participants in 12 simulator sessions, the index followed fatigue beyond elapsed time (0.32, p=0.002) and, at a 10% false-positive alarm setting, detected 91% of 'fighting sleep' minutes versus 33% for camera PERCLOS, alarming about three minutes before the first such rating in the laboratory and nine minutes before sleep onset in a parked-car test.

papers.title: Preconditioning with Menaquinone-7 and Environmental Enrichment Produces Distinct Osteocalcin and Neuroplasticity Responses Following Chronic Social Defeat Stress.
papers.summary: This study examined four-week preconditioning with menaquinone-7 (vitamin K2, 100 µg), environmental enrichment, or both before 10-day chronic social defeat stress in male C57BL/6N mice, focusing on the osteocalcin bone-brain axis and neuroplasticity markers. CSDS reduced serum and brain undercarboxylated osteocalcin, Bdnf expression, BDNF, GAP43, and MAP2; MK-7 and EE each improved behavioral and cognitive outcomes, with MK-7 showing broader effects on ucOC- and BDNF-related markers and only outcome-specific MK-7×EE interactions.

papers.title: Delayed Declarative and Procedural Memory Performance Following Interference: A Comparison of a 90-Min Midday Nap, Quiet Rest, and Active Wake.
papers.summary: This study compared a 90-min midday nap, quiet rest, and active wake for delayed declarative and procedural memory after interference learning in 37 habitual nappers, using post-interference performance as baseline. No significant group or group×time effects emerged, though exploratory within-group analyses showed procedural improvements and nap-group EEG-memory associations (e.g., frontal N2 slow spindle density with next-day declarative accuracy).

papers.title: A Multi-View Graph Convolutional Network with Context Gating for Frequency-Aware Sleep Stage Classification.
papers.summary: Proposes DCMG-Net, a dual-branch CNN and context-gated multi-view graph convolutional network for five-class EEG-only sleep staging that fuses functional, learnable, and physiological frequency-band graph views. Reported overall accuracies of 91.2%, 90.0%, and 86.3% on Sleep-EDF-20, ISRUC-S3, and SHHS, with context gating improving macro-F1 over direct concatenation by 6.1 and 2.3 points on ISRUC-S3 and SHHS.

papers.title: Operational Definitions of Transition Onset Shape EEG Biomarker Timing in Drowsiness: A Single-Channel Method Comparison.
papers.summary: Developed a benchmarking framework applying seven onset estimators and 32 features to single-channel frontal EEG drowsiness data (17 participants), with external replication in DROZY, to test how operational onset definitions shape lead times against a null. Estimator choice shifted onsets by minutes and changed detection coverage from 45% to 100%; no estimator showed a detectable excess of onsets in the final 150 s before the anchor, and adding EEG to session time gave no detectable improvement.

papers.title: Exploratory Assessment of Portable EEG- and PPG-Derived Indices Following High-Intensity Exercise Under Partial Sleep Restriction in Young Men.
papers.summary: Exploratory randomized study comparing 20 young men under normal sleep (~8 h) versus partial sleep restriction (~4 h) on portable prefrontal EEG and PPG indices, heart rate recovery, and perceived exertion after the Harvard Step Test. Sleep restriction showed a group × time increase in theta-to-beta ratio (Holm p = 0.034), altered HRV/sympathetic/parasympathetic indices, higher recovery heart rate, lower HRR, and higher RPE.

papers.title: EEG Theta Power as an Indicator of Cognitive Workload in Student Pilots.
papers.summary: Recorded EEG from eight scalp locations in ten student pilots during baseline and three flight-simulation modules of differing difficulty in a high-fidelity PC-21 simulator, alongside NASA-TLX ratings. Theta power was higher in the most demanding phase (frontal, temporal, occipital regions), but correlations between subjective workload and theta measures were weak and not significant at the group level.

papers.title: Neurocognitive and Behavioural Correlates of REM-Predominant Obstructive Sleep Apnoea.
papers.summary: Compared neurocognitive and behavioural profiles of REM-predominant OSA (REM AHI/NREM AHI ≥2) versus NREM-predominant OSA in patients with suspected OSA, using a neuropsychological battery and questionnaires. Among 74 moderate-to-severe patients, 13 met REM-OSA criteria and showed longer TMT-A, TMT-B, and TMT B-A times and higher impulsivity after adjustment, despite lower overall AHI and oxygen desaturation index.

papers.title: tACS and nervonic acid inhibit microglial overactivation via the Rap1 signaling pathway and ameliorate sleep deprivation-induced cognitive impairment.
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived mice, transcranial alternating current stimulation improved memory and cognition while inhibiting microglial phagocytosis, increasing synaptic density, and reducing neuronal apoptosis. Metabolomics implicated nervonic acid and the Rap1 pathway, and nervonic acid administration suppressed LPS-induced microglial overactivation and alleviated cognitive impairment in sleep-deprived mice.

papers.title: Objective-to-Subjective Sleep Discrepancy in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Pilot EEG Study.
papers.summary: In 22 hospitalized rheumatoid arthritis patients, subjective total sleep time exceeded single-channel EEG-derived sleep time by a median of 82.75 minutes and the two measures were not correlated. Greater sleep discrepancy was associated with lower albumin, higher CRP, glucocorticoid use, higher DAS28-CRP, greater disability, and non-dipper nocturnal blood pressure patterns.

papers.title: Evaluating Autonomic and Cognitive Responses to Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation as a Countermeasure for Sleep Deprivation.
papers.summary: In a double-blind study of 19 participants undergoing 26 h of continuous wakefulness, a single 30-min tDCS session over the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex had no significant main effect on cognitive performance or heart rate variability versus sham. Only exploratory stimulation × window interactions within the MATB and lower self-reported sleepiness were observed, without a corresponding performance benefit.

papers.title: Visual function and circadian rest-activity rhythms in US older adults: The National Health and Aging Trends Study.
papers.summary: In 728 older US adults from NHATS with objective vision assessments and accelerometry, poorer distance acuity, near acuity, and contrast sensitivity were associated with lower rest-activity rhythm amplitude and percent rhythm, but not with mesor, acrophase, or alpha. Function-on-scalar regression showed lower daytime and higher nighttime activity among those with vision impairment.

papers.title: Short-video addiction and circadian phase delay in Chinese adolescents and emerging adults: A three-wave longitudinal study with a nested dim-light melatonin assessment.
papers.summary: In a three-wave longitudinal cohort of 1660 Chinese students with nested dim-light melatonin assessments, short-video addiction scores were associated with circadian phase delay, and the per-SD phase-delay association strengthened from middle school to university (0.92 vs. 2.15 hours). In an extreme-group subsample, health behaviors mediated 65.7% of the association, with dominant pathways shifting from physical activity to sleep quality/diet to psychological stress across educational stages.

papers.title: Quantitative EEG Differences Across Two Sedation Conditions in a Child with Epilepsy: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A single pediatric case report compared duration-matched quantitative EEG in a child with structural epilepsy under propofol versus chloral hydrate sedation, observing higher spike frequency (14.11 vs 4.12 spikes/min) and spike index (84.95% vs 27.96%) with chloral hydrate and greater delta predominance with propofol, while cautioning that the recordings were about a year apart and not attributable to the agents.

papers.title: Guipi Tang Combined with Probiotics Ameliorates Sleep Deprivation-Induced Hippocampal Injury and Pentobarbital-Induced Sleep Alterations in Mice.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of sleep deprivation, combined Guipi Tang plus probiotics improved pentobarbital-induced sleep responses and hippocampal injury relative to individual treatments, accompanied by altered gut microbial composition, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β), increased autophagy markers (ATG5, Beclin-1, LC3-II), decreased p62, and a raised Bcl-2/Bax ratio with fewer TUNEL-positive cells.

papers.title: Chronic Sleep Deprivation-Induced Anxiety-Like Behaviors Correlate With Altered Peripheral S100A10+ Immune Cells and Hippocampal Metabolic Dysregulation.
papers.summary: Seven days of chronic sleep deprivation in mice produced anxiety-like behaviors alongside a shift toward pro-inflammatory Ly6C-high monocytes, upregulated S100A10 in CD45+ leukocytes, CD8+ T cells and monocytes, disrupted blood-brain barrier integrity, microglial activation, and 157 differential hippocampal metabolites enriched in cAMP signaling and glutathione metabolism pathways.

papers.title: Self-generated action shapes theta phase alignment at encoding and later recollection
papers.summary: Three preregistered human experiments dissociating choice, movement, and outcome control during scene encoding showed that choosing improved recognition, especially recollection over familiarity, and increased action-onset-locked theta and alpha inter-trial phase coherence, with later posterior theta alignment (353–570 ms) predicting Remember versus Know responses.

papers.title: Circadian Disruption and the 24-Hour Blood Pressure Phenotype in Arterial Hypertension.
papers.summary: This review frames circadian disruption as a multidimensional determinant of hypertension and proposes the 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure profile as an integrated downstream phenotype, noting that controlled studies support causal effects of acute circadian misalignment while free-living evidence is mostly observational and randomized trials do not support universal bedtime antihypertensive dosing.

papers.title: Age-Adjusted Exploratory Analysis of Spectral, Aperiodic, and Microstate Electroencephalography Features in Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.summary: In an age-adjusted exploratory analysis of resting-state 128-channel EEG from the BrainLat dataset (32 MS patients, 32 controls), global aperiodic offset showed the strongest diagnosis association after FDR correction (β = 1.816, q = 3.29×10⁻⁷), while global central frequency, exponent, power spectral density, and all microstate measures did not survive correction. However, non-overlapping age ranges (21–55 vs 56–83 years) mean the diagnosis coefficient depends on extrapolation and cannot establish an MS-specific effect.

papers.title: Zhibai Anshen Oral Liquid Activates cAMP/PKA/CREB Signaling Axis and Promotes BDNF and Circadian Clock Protein Expression to Ameliorate Insomnia.
papers.summary: Using PCPA-induced insomnia rats combined with RNA-seq and network pharmacology, the authors identified 151 candidate ZBAS targets and found that the anti-insomnia effects of Zhibai Anshen oral liquid were associated with activation of the cAMP/PKA/CREB axis and upregulation of BDNF and circadian clock proteins (PER3, CLOCK); the adenylyl cyclase inhibitor MDL12330A attenuated these effects.

papers.title: Sex-Stratified Associations Between Sleep-Stage-Specific Respiratory Indices and Metabolic Parameters in Children with Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cross-sectional secondary analysis of 514 children with suspected sleep-disordered breathing, triglycerides were positively associated with all six respiratory indices in both sexes, and significant sex interactions indicated stronger triglycerides–OAHI associations in girls for whole-night and NREM OAHI; no other interactions survived FDR correction.

papers.title: Immediate responses to stimulation of trigeminal-associated sites using conventional suction-type and wearable silicone SSP electrodes: An exploratory randomized three-arm study in healthy adults.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.summary: In an exploratory randomized three-arm study of 54 healthy young adults, silicone SSP stimulation produced a greater pre-to-post increase in Karolinska Sleepiness Scale scores than no-current control (mean difference 2.389), but superiority or equivalence versus conventional SSP was not established, and no significant time×group interactions appeared for EEG, HRV, or EMG.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture Ameliorates Circadian Rhythm Disruption-Induced Oligoasthenospermia in Mice by Modulating the Sirt1/Nrf2 Antioxidant Signaling Pathway.
papers.summary: Combining bioinformatic hub-gene screening (IL1B, NFE2L2, PCNA, DMPK, MYH9) with a chronic jet lag mouse model, this study found that electroacupuncture reversed circadian disruption-induced sperm quality impairment, restored hepatic clock rhythmicity, and upregulated the testicular Sirt1/Nrf2 antioxidant pathway.

papers.title: Effects of Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation over the Left Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex on Executive Function During Sustained Simulated Flight Operations: A Randomized Crossover Study Using a Flight-Cognitive Dual-Task Paradigm.
papers.summary: In a randomized, sham-controlled crossover study of 25 healthy men, active iTBS over the left DLPFC shortened 3-back reaction time and improved 3-back and rule-switching accuracy during a simulated flight dual-task paradigm, without effects on Go/No-Go performance. Exploratory EEG microstate and fNIRS changes accompanied these working memory and switching improvements.

papers.title: Detecting cognitive motor dissociation in unresponsive brain-injured patients: a prospective cohort study using active task-based EEG.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 56 clinically unresponsive brain-injured patients, active task-based EEG during motor imagery detected cognitive motor dissociation in 6 patients (10.7%). CMD-positive patients descriptively showed more favorable 6-month outcomes and no deaths, though group differences were not statistically significant.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythms, Exercise, and Metabolic Remodeling in MASLD: From Chronometabolism to Muscle-Preserving Care.
papers.summary: This critical narrative review integrates clinical, metabolomics, and mechanistic evidence on circadian regulation, exercise, and muscle-preserving care in MASLD. It concludes that no universal optimal exercise timing has been established and that timed metabolite signatures require standardized sampling and external validation before informing clinical decisions.

papers.title: EEG morphology and peri-ictal MRI abnormalities in status epilepticus and ictal-interictal continuum.
papers.summary: In a single-center prospective cohort of 205 patients with status epilepticus or ictal-interictal continuum, excitatory-predominant EEG morphology and lateralized periodic discharges were associated with increased risk of peri-ictal DWI/FLAIR MRI abnormalities. The number of excitatory features correlated with the extent of affected MRI sequences.

papers.title: From hemodynamics to function: the role of fNIRS and hybrid EEG-fNIRS systems in next-generation assistive technologies for rehabilitation.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines fNIRS and hybrid EEG-fNIRS systems as control modalities for next-generation rehabilitation assistive technologies, including BCIs, prostheses, and wheelchairs. It argues that hybrid EEG-fNIRS combines high temporal resolution with spatial and hemodynamic information to improve accuracy and reduce false positives.

papers.title: Identification of Hypoxia- and Circadian Rhythm-Related Prognostic Genes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Through Integrative Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analysis.
papers.summary: Integrated TCGA/GEO transcriptomic analysis, LASSO and random survival forest modeling identified four hypoxia- and circadian rhythm-related prognostic genes (ADM, PFKFB3, SERPINE1, RORA) in hepatocellular carcinoma, with a risk model stratifying patients by survival and single-cell/IHC validation showing elevated ADM and PFKFB3 protein in tumor tissue.

papers.title: Decision-Aligned Value Learning for Selective Adoption of EEG Fusion in Human-Robot Collaboration
papers.summary: Proposed VECTA, a sample-wise value-estimation framework that decides when EEG-informed fusion predictions should replace base predictions in human-robot collaboration, using signed gain learning under budget constraints. Across three HRC datasets, estimated gains correlated with realized gains (Spearman 0.347-0.612) and VECTA reduced Brier loss and harmful fusion adoption, with direct post-hoc applicability to external multimodal datasets.

papers.title: Depression is associated with endometrial polyp occurrence and convergent gut microbiota-mitochondrial alterations: a multi-omics case-control study.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: A multi-omics case-control study (n=466 cohort; 16S rRNA and RNA-seq in 30 participants) plus a chronic restraint stress mouse model found depression associated with higher endometrial polyp odds (OR 2.28) and convergent gut microbiota-mitochondrial alterations, including reduced electron-transfer/oxidative phosphorylation signals, higher Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and lower Eggerthella lenta, with F. prausnitzii supplementation linked to higher uterine TOMM20 and lower proliferation in stressed mice.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
